newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan warlord won't bomb Kabul civilians again.
newsitem.headline: Afghan warlord won't bomb Kabul civilians again.

text.p: Powerful northern Afghan Uzbek chief Abdul Rashid Dostum assured a senior U.N. envoy on Sunday that his jets would not bomb civilian targets in the capital Kabul while fighting the Taleban militia.

Under-Secretary General for Humanitarian Affairs Yasushi Akashi complained to Dostum about an air raid earlier this month that killed at least four people in Kabul, which is ruled by the Taleban Islamic movement.
Dostum, talking through an interpreter, acknowledged that the January 5 raid by two jets of his air force was "a mistake" and said there was no intention to bomb the civilian population.
He assured Akashi that "this will not be repeated in the future".
But he said the Taleban, fighting a coalition of Dostum's forces and those loyal to ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani, should also refrain from attacking civilian targets.

Akashi was in Mazar-i-Sharif to meet Dostum in a day's trip to Afghanistan as part of preparations for a U.N.-sponsored conference in the Turkmen capital of Ashgabat on January 21-22 to discuss future aid for this war-devastated country.
